Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Education | Regional Prof. Francis Kwaw Andoh inducted as Principal of Enchi College of Education Source : Augustine Boah 22 November 2026 5:20pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Prof. Francis Kwaw Andoh, an alumnus of Enchi College of Education, has been formally inducted as the new Principal of the institution in the Western North Region.
His investiture took place on November 20, 2026, at the college's auditorium, bringing together political leaders, traditional authorities, educationists, businesspeople, family members, colleagues, lecturers and students.
He succeeds Professor Philip Ntaah, who led the college from 2019 to 2025.
Among the dignitaries present were the Omanhene of the Aowin Traditional Area, Beyeman Tano Kwaw Benbuin III; Director-General of the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC), Professor Ahmed Jinapor Abdulai; and Chairman of the college's Governing Council, Dr Frank Kwekucher Ackah.
Professor Andoh is an economist, researcher and academic whose career spans classroom teaching, university administration, research and international development consultancy.
He began his professional career as a classroom teacher at Dadieso Primary School in Suaman, where he worked from 1997 to 1999. He later taught at Nkoranza Senior High/Technical School between 2002 and 2005 and Efutu Senior High/Technical School in 2006.
He obtained a bachelor's degree in Economics from the University of Cape Coast (UCC) in 2002, followed by an MPhil in Economics from the same university in 2008.
In 2010, he earned a Certificate in Cost Analysis in Education from UNESCO's International Institute for Educational Planning in Paris.
He subsequently received an international scholarship from the African Economic Research Consortium, sponsored by the World Bank, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the Canadian Government, to pursue a PhD in Economics at the University of Dar es Salaam in Tanzania. He completed the programme in 2017.
His academic career at UCC began in 2007 as a Senior Research Assistant. He later became a Principal Research Assistant before moving into lecturing in 2010. He was promoted to Senior Lecturer in 2020 and appointed Associate Professor in February 2024.
At UCC, he also held several administrative positions, including Hall Tutor, Senior Hall Tutor and Hall Master of Atlantic Hall. He further served as Dean of the School of Economics before taking up his new role at Enchi College of Education.
Beyond academia, Professor Andoh has undertaken consultancy assignments for international organisations, including the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation, United Nations Population Fund, International Labour Organisation, Copenhagen Consensus Centre, Solidaridad West Africa and SNV Netherlands Development Organisation.
In 2019, he was appointed a Visiting Scholar at the IMF in Washington, DC, where he participated in research and academic discussions on fiscal and economic policy issues.
His research interests include macroeconomics, public finance, public policy and health economics, with particular focus on fiscal policy, public debt, healthcare financing, health insurance, foreign direct investment, inequality and multidimensional poverty.
He has also supervised and co-supervised doctoral and master's students, many of whom have gone on to occupy professional positions in Ghana and abroad.
Speaking after his induction, Professor Andoh said he would draw on his academic experience, professional networks and leadership skills to strengthen the college and advance teacher education in Ghana.
He called on staff to support his administration and work collectively towards the development of the institution and the training of teachers.
Professor Ahmed Jinapor Abdulai, in his remarks, commended the college for its recent performance and urged the lecturers, Governing Council and staff to rally behind the new Principal to drive further progress.
He also assured the institution that GTEC would collaborate with the Ghana Education Trust Fund (GETFund) to facilitate the completion of abandoned projects on campus and the renovation of the college's auditorium.
Professor Andoh's appointment brings to Enchi College of Education an academic with experience in teaching, research, institutional administration and international development work.
